title: Add workload presets for top hosted models + standard experiment matrix generator
author: Rina Kobayashi
body:
Motivation: For the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint we need repeatable, apples-to-apples end-to-end runs that reflect real hosted traffic shapes (prompt length distributions, concurrency, streaming vs non-streaming, decode params). Today, benchmark-lab configs are too ad hoc: each run encodes slightly different workloads, which makes regression detection and cross-GPU comparisons noisy.

This PR introduces: (1) versioned workload presets for our top hosted model families, and (2) a standard experiment matrix generator that expands presets x models x GPUs x quant modes into validated run configs with consistent metadata.

What’s in this PR (high level): Adds workload preset library: A small set of named presets under workloads/presets/ (yaml) that cover common hosted shapes: chat_streaming_mixed (mixed prompt lengths, streaming on, concurrency tuned to saturate decode), chat_nonstreaming_prefill_heavy (long prompts, shorter generation), completions_decode_heavy (short prompt, longer gen), embeddings_burst (high QPS, small payload) (embeddings runner landing separately, but preset is included for forward compatibility). Each preset includes: prompt_length_distribution (quantiles + weights), max_input_tokens / max_output_tokens, temperature/top_p, stop sequences, concurrency, ramp/warmup, duration, and batching hints.

Adds "top hosted" model mapping: Introduces models/top_hosted.yaml that maps model IDs to a family tag (llama/qwen/mistral), default decoding params, and which presets are valid (e.g., some models we don’t want in very-long-context runs yet).

Adds matrix generator: New CLI benchctl gen-matrix that takes: --models (or --model-set=top_hosted), --gpus (a100|h100|h200|l40s), --quant (fp16|fp8|int8), --presets, plus a couple of guardrails: cap on total generated runs, and an explicit "dangerous" flag for generating huge matrices. Output is a directory of run configs, plus a manifest.json that captures expansion inputs and a stable matrix_id.

Validation & determinism: Adds schema validation for presets and generated configs (pydantic), stable ordering when expanding combinations, and explicit pinning hooks for runtime_commit and container_digest (pass-through; actual pin enforcement lives in PR #412).

Metadata tags: Ensures every generated run config includes the tags we need downstream: model_family, preset_name, quant_mode, gpu_sku, and an experiment_group string that can be used by dashboards/canary.

Docs: Adds docs/workloads.md with guidance on choosing presets, how to add a new preset safely, and how to interpret concurrency settings. Also adds examples under examples/matrices/.

Example usage:
- Generate a minimal nightly canary matrix: benchctl gen-matrix --model-set=top_hosted --gpus=h100 --quant=fp16,fp8,int8 --presets=chat_streaming_mixed --out=out/matrix_nightly
- Generate full sprint matrix (interactive): benchctl gen-matrix --model-set=top_hosted --gpus=a100,h100,h200,l40s --quant=fp16,fp8,int8 --presets=chat_streaming_mixed,chat_nonstreaming_prefill_heavy,completions_decode_heavy --max-runs=240 --out=out/matrix_sprint

Notes / decisions:
- Preset names are intentionally product-y and stable; we should treat them as API since they’ll appear in reports/dashboards.
- Prompt distributions are currently represented as weighted buckets (token_count ranges) rather than raw prompt corpora; this keeps configs lightweight and allows different prompt sets to plug in later.
- Concurrency is specified as a target range (min/max) in presets; generator resolves to a concrete concurrency value via a policy (default: midpoint) so we can later tune per GPU without changing the preset semantics.

Test plan:
- unit: schema validation for presets and matrix expansion; golden tests for deterministic ordering and manifest content.
- integration (CI): generate a small matrix and run the "config validate" command against all generated configs.

Risk:
- Low runtime risk; this is harness/config only. Biggest risk is breaking downstream consumers of config fields; mitigated by keeping old fields and adding new ones additively.

Follow-ups:
- Wire these presets into the end-to-end streaming runner (PR #413) and nightly canary job (perf-canary PRs).
- Add an explicit "prompt_set" concept (corpuses) once we finalize which prompt artifacts are safe to store and how we version them.

Screenshots/Artifacts: Attached in comments: sample generated manifest and 3 configs for llama/qwen on H100 (fp16/fp8/int8).
commits: benchctl: add gen-matrix command + deterministic expansion
workloads: add preset schema + initial top hosted presets
models: add top_hosted model set mapping + family tagging
docs: workloads presets + matrix generation how-to
tests: golden fixtures for matrix manifest + validation
conversation: Noah Patel (review): The preset definitions look good. Two concerns: (1) concurrency should not be a single value in the preset if we expect GPU-specific tuning; (2) please ensure we tag model_family + preset_name in the generated configs so dashboards can group consistently.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Agree. I changed concurrency to a min/max range in the preset and added a generator policy to pick a concrete value (default midpoint, overridable via --concurrency-policy). Also added required tags: model_family, preset_name, quant_mode, gpu_sku, experiment_group.

Claire Dubois (review): The distribution format is readable, but please document how bucketed prompt lengths map to actual prompts. Also suggest a deterministic ordering for combinations to avoid diff churn in generated configs.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Added docs/workloads.md section "How distributions are used" (bucket->sampler; prompt corpora plugged in by runner). Implemented stable ordering (models, gpus, quant, presets) and added a golden determinism test.

Sean Gallagher (review): Small: please cap matrix size by default; we’ve had people accidentally generate thousands of runs and hammer the lab scheduler. Also add a manifest field with the original args so we can debug later.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Added --max-runs default 120 with hard failure, and --allow-large-matrix to override. Manifest now records generator args, benchctl version, and a stable matrix_id.
Isabella Rossi (review): Can we add a prefill-heavy preset that specifically stresses long context? That’s where we’ve seen FP8 oddities.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Added chat_nonstreaming_prefill_heavy with long prompt buckets and shorter generation. Marked it unsupported for a couple of models in models/top_hosted.yaml pending eval signoff.
Noah Patel (review): Looks good now. Approved.
Merge bot: Squash and merge completed.
release_notes: Benchmark harness: introduced versioned workload presets for top hosted models and a matrix generator CLI to produce consistent experiment configs across GPUs/quant modes.
